method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the Rules are applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer); r 1.61 and business days in one date module, the rules in another, the questions in a seat module importing them; two regulative rules (rr 16.32, 25.04) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain dates; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Federal Court Rules 2011 (Cth), Compilation No. 11 (compilation date 11 June 2026, register id F2026C00512, includes amendments up to F2026L00616), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/F2011L01551.txt, retrieved 2026-11-06. Amendments after the compilation date are not in the text.
license: Apache-2.0 for the L4; the quoted text is (c) Commonwealth of Australia, CC BY 4.0, based on content from the Federal Register of Legislation; see SOURCE-LICENSE.md
seat: the individual party to a claim in the Federal Court: usually the applicant who brings it (an injured person, employee, person discriminated against, claimant for compensation or a debt), and the same person where the Rules put a step on the one answering (a respondent filing a defence, a respondent to an appeal, the party paying a costs bill) (fcr-seat.l4)
focus: courts, procedure, time limits, damages, costs

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run fcr-dates.l4 ; l4 run fcr-rules.l4 ; l4 run fcr-seat.l4 ; l4 run fcr-cases.l4
checks.result: 196 assertions written, 196 satisfied, 1 #TRACE FULFILLED, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics were read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: In: rr 1.61, 2.25(3), 5.22, 5.23(2), 8.02(1), 8.03(2) item 4 and (3), 8.05(1)-(2), 8.06, 10.32, 16.32, 16.33, 23.21, 25.04, 25.05(3), 25.07, 25.08, 25.09(1), 25.12, 25.13(2) (cut-off), 25.14, 26.01(3), 26.12(2), (4), (7), 26.14, 26.15, 30.41(1), 30.42, 30.43, 35.13, 35.15, 36.03, 36.04(2), 36.07, 36.10, 36.22, 36.24, 39.02, 39.03(2), 39.04, 39.05, 39.06, 40.04, 40.08, 40.13, 40.21, 40.23(4), 40.32(1), 40.33(1), 40.34(4), with the Dictionary's business day and file. Out: the machinery (Parts 1, 3, 4, 6, 43), pre-action orders (Part 7), party mechanics (Part 9; Division 9.3 is in the Federal Court of Australia Act baseline), service mechanics and other interlocutory procedure (Parts 10-22, 24, 27-29), security for costs (Part 19, the respondent's application under s 56 of the Act), special classes of proceeding (Chapter 3), the rest of Parts 25, 26, 30, 35, 36, 39 and 40, enforcement and contempt (Parts 41, 42). Reasons in NOTES.md.
